name: TouchBistro
oneLiner: iPad-based restaurant POS and management system with built-in sales reporting and analytics plus add-ons for payments, online ordering, reservations, inventory and labor; owned by Harris (Constellation Software) since July 2026.
bestFor: Independent full-service restaurants and small multi-location groups that want sales, menu and staff reporting built into their POS instead of a separate BI tool.

customers.name: Café Crêpe (multi-location group with central commissary)

updates.text: Harris, an operating group of Constellation Software, acquired TouchBistro and said it plans to keep investing in the product; the TouchBistro team joined Harris. Terms were not disclosed (The Globe and Mail reported about $100 million).

features: Real-time sales reports by time period, menu item and staff member, viewable from the cloud
Menu mix and item performance analysis
Table management and iPad-based order taking for full-service restaurants
Add-ons for online ordering, reservations, kitchen display, loyalty and marketing

pricing.text: Point of Sale software from $69/month per location (hardware sold separately); Essentials bundle with payments and hardware listed from $119/month on the pricing page (the homepage has shown $99/month). Add-ons such as online ordering and kitchen display cost extra; enterprise is quoted.

notes: Acquisition: Harris (Constellation Software) announced it acquired TouchBistro on July 7, 2026; product continues to be sold under the TouchBistro name. Harris says it powers 16,000+ restaurants in 100+ countries (vendor figure). Pricing comes from search snippets of touchbistro.com (not fetched); $119 vs $99 for the Essentials bundle conflicts between pages, so re-check. Dropped from current review: 'POS software typically starts in the low hundreds per month per location' (published entry price is $69/month). No 2025 product launch confirmed; no AI reporting feature confirmed, so it fits an 'AI agents' list only loosely as a POS reporting option. Customer case studies are vendor-published; their percentages (e.g. Café Crêpe 85% less inventory time, Uncle Tetsu 11% less waste) are vendor-reported.
